I farm a small 2.6 mu wheat-maize rotation with well irrigation, so I will keep the whole plot in the usual cycle and manage it carefully rather than taking big risks. Because my land is small and some family labor is tied up off-farm, I will use practices that are reliable, not too labor-heavy, and that protect yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer in early, irrigate at key stages, and keep field work simple with rotary tillage. For maize, I will also use improved seed, feed it a bit more nitrogen than wheat, use fewer irrigations because I have a summer crop and access to a well, and control pests only as needed. I want steady grain output from both seasons, so I will stay with the wheat-maize system I know well and make sure inputs are enough to support yield but not excessive for such a small farm.
